notes: FOUR CONTROLS THAT WERE NEVER THERE: PAYROLL APPROVAL, FUND RESTRICTION, BUDGET OVERRIDE EVIDENCE, AND A DUE DATE ON AN ADVANCE. Three of these are not bugs. Nothing was computed wrongly, the answer simply did not exist, which is why looking for what is broken would never have found them. PAYROLL IS APPROVED BY SOMEBODY OTHER THAN WHOEVER RAN IT. A payroll month went straight from draft to posted with no second signature at any amount. That was a side effect rather than carelessness: payroll is deliberately exempt from the payment approval tiers, because a threshold must never be able to hold up the month's salaries, and nothing was put in its place. Employee records are editable by the same people, so one officer could add a person, set their pay, run the month and post it with nobody else involved, and it is the largest recurring outflow most months. There is now an APPROVE step before POST, and until it is given there is no Post button at all. The month is approved WHOLE, because approving some payslips and not others would mean a part paid payroll. The person who ran it cannot approve it, counted across the payslips, so a month two people ran needs an approver who is neither of them. REOPEN FOR CORRECTION returns it to draft and WITHDRAWS the approval, so corrected figures cannot ride in on a signature given for different ones. One exception, recorded rather than hidden: where there is no other finance user at all, requiring a second person would not create dual control, it would stop payroll running and push an office of one towards a shared login. There the approval is allowed and the audit trail says so. The screen names who approved the month and when. A RESTRICTED FUND MEANS SOMETHING BEFORE THE MONEY GOES. Fund balances by restriction already existed on the reports and already flagged an overspent restricted fund, but only after the fact. Will this take a restricted fund past what the donor gave us is the first question a donor audit asks. Posting a voucher that would do so now asks first, naming the fund, the donor, where it stands and where it would end up. Only funds the posting would actually push past their income are named: asking about one that can bear the charge would train you to click past the ones that matter. Designated and unrestricted funds do not raise it, because money the organisation set aside itself carries no promise to anyone outside it. It is a warning and never a refusal, since a finance office legitimately commits ahead of a grant arriving. And whether or not anybody was asked, every posting that leaves a restricted fund overspent is written to the audit trail, so it does not depend on which screen the payment came from. A BUDGET OVERRIDE LEAVES A RECORD. Raising a commitment above the available budget has always asked whether to raise it anyway, and that question is right. What it did not do was leave a trace, so budget utilisation as a headline figure could not tell a budget respected from a budget overridden. Each commitment raised over the line now carries how far over it was, with the availability, the amount and who decided it on the audit trail, and the Budgets screen lists them. The figure is measured against availability as it stood BEFORE the commitment existed, which is what you were shown when you were asked. AN ADVANCE HAS A DATE IT IS DUE BACK. There was no due date anywhere on the record, so unretired advances could only be reported as one undifferentiated total: nothing could age them, nothing could say which were late, nobody could be sent a list. That is how such a figure accumulates, not through anyone's decision but because there was no way to say an advance is overdue. Advances now carry a DUE BACK date from a policy period after the advance date, and the list shows how far past it each one is. The period is a setting, because it is a policy and thirty days is a common rule rather than a fact. Advances already on your books have been given one on the same basis, so the ageing covers what is outstanding today rather than starting empty. A part retired advance is chased for the remainder only, and a retired or written off one leaves the list. INSTALLING: this version adds tables and checks to your ledger, so it is not a pure code update. It installs straight over the previous version and your data is migrated in place, but please take a backup first: Backup and Export, Back up now. ONE THING TO DO AFTER INSTALLING: if more than one person uses the ledger, agree who approves payroll before the next run, because it cannot be whoever runs it.
